lead: Diesel knock is the hard, metallic combustion noise of a CI engine when ignition delay is too long. Fuel injected during the delay has time to mix with air and collect. When ignition finally starts, this collected fuel burns fast in the premixed phase. Pressure rises sharply, the block rings, and we hear knock. The idea matters for engine noise, durability and efficiency. Only a few universities teach this topic in detail. You meet it in diesel generators, trucks and some cars, especially during cold starts or with poor fuel.
prereq: You need: the four CI combustion stages and delay period from Chapter 3.5, and the difference between knock and pre-ignition from Chapter 3.3.

blocks.text: Long ignition delay starts the chain. Fuel injected during delay mixes with hot air but does not burn. More fuel collects as a premixed cloud. Autoignition then starts at many points and the cloud burns fast. Pressure rises sharply in a short crank angle. The pressure wave hits the chamber walls and we hear the hard diesel knock.

Normal CI combustion has a small premixed spike. A long delay makes the spike large. Peak pressure and rate of pressure rise increase. This adds noise and mechanical stress. The spike is worst at cold start, when the air charge is cool.

Diesel knock is not spark knock. Spark knock starts after the spark and comes from end-gas autoignition (Chapter 3.3). Diesel knock starts at the end of a long delay and comes from too much premixed fuel. Pre-ignition also starts before the spark.
Delay depends on fuel ignition quality, air temperature, injection timing, spray quality and chamber design.

items: Higher cetane number: cetane measures ignition quality. A higher value shortens delay. Add a cetane booster to diesel.
Retarded injection: start injection later, closer to top dead centre where air is hotter. This cuts delay and peak pressure. Too much retard raises exhaust temperature and lowers efficiency.
Warmer intake air: a glow plug or intake heater shortens chemical delay at cold start. Cold diesel generators in hill areas often need this.
Pilot injection: a small early spray starts a flame. The main spray then burns after a short delay.
Better atomization: high injection pressure and a clean nozzle make fine drops that vaporise fast.
Chamber design: hot walls and organised air motion help mixing. Avoid fuel hitting cold walls. See Chapters 3.7 and 3.8.

blocks.where: θ is delay in crank degrees, N is engine speed in rpm, t is delay in ms.

figure.caption: Long ignition delay lets fuel collect; the resulting fast premixed burn raises pressure and produces diesel knock. A cetane booster shortens the first step.

spec.title: Diesel knock chain

examples.question: A diesel engine runs at 1500 rpm. Ignition delay is 1.4 ms. Find the delay in crank degrees. Raising cetane number from 45 to 50 cuts delay to 1.0 ms. Find the reduction in crank degrees.
steps: Use θ = 0.006 N t, with θ in crank degrees, N in rpm and t in ms.
At N = 1500 rpm, 0.006 × 1500 = 9.0 degrees per ms.
For t = 1.4 ms: θ₁ = 9.0 × 1.4 = 12.6 crank degrees.
For t = 1.0 ms: θ₂ = 9.0 × 1.0 = 9.0 crank degrees.
examples.answer: The delay is 12.6 crank degrees at 1.4 ms, 9.0 crank degrees at 1.0 ms, and the reduction is 3.6 crank degrees.
examples.check:
N=1500
t1=1.4
t2=1.0
a=0.006*N*t1
b=0.006*N*t2
print(round(a,1))
print(round(b,1))
print(round(a-b,1))

traps: Diesel knock is not spark knock. It comes from long ignition delay and too much premixed fuel, not from a spark.
Cetane number is for diesel ignition quality. Octane number is for petrol knock resistance. Do not swap them.
Retarding injection reduces knock but too much retard lowers efficiency and raises exhaust temperature.
A long delay is the cause, not the cure. A short delay gives a small premixed spike and quieter combustion.
Knock is judged by rate of pressure rise; peak pressure alone can mislead.

quiz.a: It is the hard combustion noise from a rapid premixed burn after a long ignition delay in a CI engine.

quiz.q: Why does a long ignition delay cause knock?
quiz.a: More fuel mixes and collects during delay. It then autoignites at many points and burns fast, so pressure rises sharply.

quiz.q: An engine runs at 2000 rpm with delay 1.2 ms. Find delay in crank degrees.
How does a cetane booster reduce knock?
quiz.a: It shortens ignition delay, so less fuel collects before autoignition and the premixed spike is smaller.

quiz.q: State one difference between cetane and octane number.
quiz.a: Cetane measures diesel ignition quality; octane measures petrol resistance to spark knock.

quiz.q: At 1800 rpm, delay falls from 1.5 ms to 1.1 ms. Find the reduction in crank degrees.
quiz.a: Degrees per ms = 0.006 × 1800 = 10.8. Reduction = 10.8 × (1.5 − 1.1) = 4.32 crank degrees.

quiz.q: Why does pilot injection reduce diesel knock?
quiz.a: A small early spray starts a flame. The main spray then ignites after a short delay, so less fuel collects and the premixed burn is gentler.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern common-rail engines use multiple injections per cycle to shape the heat-release rate. Researchers watch the premixed spike with in-cylinder pressure sensors and optical engines. Cetane improvers and fuel additives are an active area for cold climates and poor diesel quality. Search for diesel knock, ignition delay, cetane number and pilot injection.
